column1: # Where each French noun's gender in lex-fr.tsv was read.
# The tooltip prints a noun's gender beside it, under both forms a row
# weaves. On 2026-10-08 every French noun was read against English
# Wiktionary's French entry, fetched raw, and none was wrong: 167 of the 178
# rows carry the gender of their page's one French noun, and the 11 others
# A Wiktionary page holds every word of one spelling, so a line citing it
# means the gender of this word's own noun there. Eight pages hold two:
# livre, a book, is masculine where livre, a pound, is feminine; souris, a
# mouse, feminine where souris, an archaic smile, is masculine; mari,
# husband, marin, sailor, chèvre, goat, ombre, shadow, mort, death, and
# Where Wiktionary gives one word two genders, the seed's is one of them,
# as the Old English ledger has it: enfant, child, and médecin, doctor, are
# masculine or feminine by the person meant ("mfbysense"), and amour, love,
# is given both. The seed prints all three "masculine". Whether a noun of
# either gender by sense should print Latin's "common" instead is a call
# tests/tools/genders.test.ts requires every noun in lex-fr.tsv to have a
# line here giving the gender the seed gives, citing the noun's own entry,
# and fails on a line outliving its noun.
# ---- drafted from English Wiktionary via kaikki.org (dump of 2026-11-09), decided_by=wiktionary, status=proposed: woven, labelled, not yet read by a person ----
